district.description: Known for its scenic landscapes and the spectacular Hogenakkal Falls on the Kaveri river, Dharmapuri has a rich history dating back to the Sangam era under the rule of Adhiyaman.

culturalEntries.title: Hogenakkal Falls and Coracle Rides
culturalEntries.shortDescription: A spectacular waterfall on the Kaveri river, famous for its medicinal baths, carbonatite rocks, and traditional circular coracle boat rides.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Often referred to as the 'Niagara of India', Hogenakkal is where the Kaveri river enters Tamil Nadu. The name means 'Smoking Rocks' in Kannada, referring to the mist created by the plunging water. The site is uniquely known for its ancient carbonatite rocks, considered some of the oldest in South Asia, and the traditional parisal (coracle) rides piloted by local boatmen through the river's gorges.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Geological formations date back millennia; traditional coracle navigation has been practiced here for centuries.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A vital ecological and cultural tourism site supporting the traditional livelihoods of local coracle operators and fisherfolk.
culturalEntries.festivalsCustoms: Aadi Perukku river festival, winter boating season
culturalEntries.traditionalCuisine: Freshly fried river fish with spicy masalas, ragi kali, meen kulambu
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: Tamil Nadu Tourism Development Corporation; Geological Survey of India reports

culturalEntries.title: Adhiyaman Kottai
culturalEntries.alternateNames: Thagadur Fort, Adhiyaman Nedumaan Anji Fortress
culturalEntries.shortDescription: Historic fortress remains linked to the legendary Sangam-era chieftain Adhiyaman Nedumaan Anji of Thagadur.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Adhiyaman Kottai is an ancient circular earthen fortress that served as the citadel of King Adhiyaman Nedumaan Anji, one of the seven great philanthropists (Kadai Ezhu Vallalgal) celebrated in classical Sangam literature (Purananuru). Adhiyaman is immortalized for gifting the rare celestial black gooseberry (nelli kani)—believed to grant longevity—to the revered poetess Avvaiyar. The site preserves ancient temple shrines and defensive moats.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Sangam period (circa 1st - 3rd century CE); praised extensively in Purananuru verse 91.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: Keeps alive the memory of classical Tamil chieftaincy, generous patron-poet friendship, and Sangam military heritage.
culturalEntries.festivalsCustoms: Avvaiyar literary commemorations and local temple festivals
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: Purananuru Sangam poetry; Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology

culturalEntries.title: Theerthamalai Theerthagiriswarar Temple
culturalEntries.shortDescription: Ancient hilltop Shiva temple near Harur renowned for its perennial sacred natural springs cascading down the cliffs.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Situated on a scenic hill near Harur, the Theerthagiriswarar Temple is believed to have Chola and Vijayanagara foundations. The temple is famed for five perennial holy water springs (theerthams)—including Agasthya Theertham, Rama Theertham, and Vasishta Theertham—flowing perpetually from the clefts of the living rockface. Pilgrims trek up the hill to bathe in the cool medicinal waters and worship Lord Shiva.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Medieval origin with inscriptional records dating to the Chola, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara eras.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A prominent regional pilgrimage center integrating nature, sacred mountain worship, and the healing powers of natural spring waters.
culturalEntries.festivalsCustoms: Maha Shivaratri, Aadi Amavasya, Panguni Uthiram
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department; District Inscription Volumes
